summary: Champions League Wednesday: 12 games researched, 4 kept (all medium confidence): Flamengo v Grêmio (Flamengo 80%), Viking v Sabah (Viking 68%), Leipzig v Man City (City 61%) and Dortmund v Betis (Dortmund 55%). Excluded: AEK v Real Madrid (GK reported differently, heavy rotation), Slavia v Arsenal (Eze doubtful, Slavia GK disputed), Fenerbahçe v Liverpool (interim coach within 14 days, unexplained move), Porto v Napoli (De Bruyne game-time decision, conflicting Napoli XIs), Lens v Como (Como GK disputed, unexplained 11% move), PSV v Club Brugge (8.6% move past the bookmaker line without news), Botafogo v Atlético-MG (conflicting reports on Danilo and the Atlético GK), Athletico-PR v Vasco (Vasco XI reported five different ways).

checks.team_news: Flamengo (Leonardo Jardim): Plata is suspended (3rd yellow). Paquetá (knee) and Danilo (jaw surgery) are out. Terra and Coluna do Fla say Alex Sandro (thigh edema) is out until after the FIFA window, while Lance lists him as a doubt; he is in no predicted XI. Carrascal is back from suspension, De La Cruz is available, and Saúl and Valencia are back in training (bench). Grêmio (Renato Portaluppi): GK Weverton and striker Carlos Vinícius are suspended. Nardoni, Pavón and Diego Caito are injured, and Danilo Barbosa and Jovane are unlikely to travel. LB Marlon (leg pain) is a doubt, but Lance names Caio Paulista the favourite to start.

They differ only at left-back (Royal per Lance/Gazeta, Ayrton per Sportsgambler/Zonamista). Grêmio (3-4-3): Gazeta and Sportsgambler agree on Grando; G. checks.rotation: Flamengo last played on 29 Oct (4-1 at Vasco), so they have 6 days' rest. They are out of the Libertadores (lost 2-3 on pens to Estudiantes on 22 Oct) and have no cup game. The next match is 18 Nov after the FIFA break, so a full-strength XI is expected. Grêmio played the Copa do Brasil semi first leg on 1 Nov (won 2-0 v Atlético-MG) and have the second leg on Saturday 7 Nov in BH. Lance says 'ainda não existe uma definição sobre possíveis preservações', with staff deciding on Wednesday. Any rotation by the underdog would only weaken Grêmio.
checks.motivation: Flamengo are 1st on 73 pts, 3 clear of Palmeiras with 5 games left after this one; a win opens a 6-point lead. Grêmio are 17th on ESPN after part of round 34 (15th and 1 pt above the Z4 per the club and Gazeta), so they are in a relegation fight but also chasing a Copa do Brasil final. It is not a derby; there is some Renato–Flamengo friction. Renato was appointed on 14 Sep and Jardim has been in charge all season, so there is no recent manager change.
checks.form: Flamengo's last 8 (all comps): W2-1 BRA, D2-2 at SAN, W1-0 FLU, D0-0 at EST, W3-0 at BAH (xG 2.95-0.51), D0-0 EST, W3-2 CAM (xG 3.09-0.99), W4-1 at VAS (xG 1.62-1.23). At home in the league they are 12W-3D-1L, GF32 GA12. FotMob season xG is 59.2 for and 32.5 against, with 73 pts against 64 expected points, so they are overperforming. Grêmio: D0-0 PAL, D1-1 at Remo, D1-1 INT, L2-4 CRU, W1-0 at CFC (xG 1.81-1.07), W2-0 CAP (xG 1.41-1.62), W2-0 CAM in the cup (24% possession, outshot 20-6). Away in the league they are 1W-5D-10L, GF10 GA23. Season xG is 36.5 for and 54.2 against.

The long-run draw rate is about 21-22% (FotMob 17-8-13; Scores24 21-10-15 in 46). In May 2026 Flamengo won 1-0 in Porto Alegre on xG 2.58-0.30 and shots 20-6. Flamengo dominate the ball, while Renato's Grêmio sit deep and rarely lose by 2+ (Sportsgambler: they covered +2 in 17 of their last 20).

games.reason: I started from Polymarket (0.836/0.107/0.057) and moved 3.6 points off the home win, adding 2.3 to the draw and 1.3 to the away win. That lands near the de-vigged bookmaker consensus (DraftKings 0.814/0.119/0.068, BetExplorer average 0.809/0.122/0.070, Bet365/Coral 0.815/0.124/0.062), which is below Polymarket on Flamengo. All three models are lower still (ValorFinal 72/18/10, KickOff 69/19/12, Vitibet 79/14/7). Reasons for the draw bump: Grêmio draw 31% of their away games (5/16) and rarely lose heavily, Flamengo's home games are low-scoring (under 3.5 in 14 of 15, 3 home draws), Flamengo overperform their xPts by 9, and they are without Plata, Paquetá, Danilo and Alex Sandro. I did not go further toward the models for these reasons. Grêmio lack their first-choice GK Weverton, striker Carlos Vinícius and three injured players. They may rest players for Saturday's Copa do Brasil semi second leg. They have 1 away win all season, and their xG is 36.5 for against 54.2 against. Flamengo are rested, have no cup games, and are in a title race. Draw at 13% is below the 25% cap, so the straight win is allowed. Confidence is medium rather than high for three reasons: Flamengo's LB starter is unsettled (Royal or Ayrton), Alex Sandro's status is reported differently (both say he won't start), and Grêmio's XI will only be set on matchday, though that uncertainty only helps Flamengo.
games.main_risk: The likeliest way Flamengo fail is a 0-0 or 1-1. Grêmio pack a deep back five as they did against Atlético-MG (24% possession, 2-0 win) and in their 5 away draws. A Flamengo side without Plata and Paquetá creates little in a low-scoring home game, and Grêmio steal one on the counter or from a set piece. There is evidence for this: Grêmio's 5/16 away draws, +2 covered in 17 of 20, and the 1-1 at the Maracanã in Aug 2025. It is already reflected in the draw at 0.13.

AEK are 1-0-2 with 3 points, around 27th, and need home points to reach the top 24. Not a derby. Mourinho has been in post since the summer and Nikolić is in place, with no change in the last 14 days. Both sides have a lot to play for.

Away: draws at Kifisia, Asteras and Levski, a win at Volos, and defeats 1-3 at Shakhtar, 1-5 at Man City and 0-2 at Panathinaikos. Real: 9 wins and 1 loss in the last 10, no draws at all this season. Away this season: won at Espanyol, Elche, Roma (4-3), Barcelona and Racing; lost at Betis and Atlético. They keep conceding away. At Racing they had 22 shots to 10 and 7 on target to 1. I couldn't get xG: Understat returned no data, FBref and Sofascore gave 403, the FotMob API gave 404, and a search turned up nothing.

games.reason: Excluded under the INSTRUCTIONS rules. (1) Reports on Real's starting goalkeeper conflict: OKDiario has Lunin with Courtois rested; Sportaragon, Defensa Central, 365Scores and SportsGambler have Courtois. Valverde's place, just back from muscle discomfort, also differs between sources, and AEK's goalkeeper (Brignoli or Strakosha) is reported differently too. (2) Mourinho has publicly talked about load and minutes management for this game, has left Güler and Tchouaméni out to rest them, and OKDiario predicts 10 changes from the Racing XI. If the game were kept, my probabilities would be 8 / 14.5 / 77.5, below the market's 80.6% on Real. Reasons: models below the market (Opta 71.6%, OddAlerts 75.3%), the DraftKings de-vig at 77.3%, a rotated and tired Real side, AEK's 6/6 home record, and both previous meetings drawn. The draw (about 14.5%) would still be under the 25% cap, so the problem is availability and rotation uncertainty, not the draw rule.
games.main_risk: AEK sit deep in a compact 4-4-2 in front of a hostile home crowd. A rotated, tired Real side (possibly with Lunin in goal and without Güler or Tchouaméni) concedes on a counter or a set piece, as it has kept doing away (4-3 at Roma, 3-2 at Elche). The result is a 1-1 or 2-2, like both previous meetings, or a late equaliser.

The draw is moved +2.4 points and Arsenal −2.4 points from the market, because Opta (18% draw, 69% Arsenal) and ClubElo (21.7%, 68%) both put the draw above the market, Saka is out and Eze is doubtful, Arsenal win narrowly (1-0, 2-0, 1-0 in the PL) and drew 2-2 at Bayern, and Slavia are unbeaten domestically and drew 2-2 at Fenerbahçe. Bookmakers (75-77% Arsenal) also sit slightly below Polymarket. The draw stays at about 17.5%, under 25%, so a straight Arsenal win at about 1.28 would otherwise be a sound leg. Strictly by the rules, though, the game is out.

Slavia have drawn 3 of their last 5 and drew 2-2 away at Fenerbahçe. Arsenal drew 2-2 at Bayern in their last UCL game and have won most PL games by one goal, so a 1-1 or a late Slavia equaliser is the most likely way the Arsenal leg fails.

games.reason: Starting from the market (0.6935 / 0.1732 / 0.1334), I shaded slightly towards the bookmakers. Both DraftKings (0.672 / 0.181) and Bet365 (0.669 / 0.187) de-vig Viking lower and the draw higher than Polymarket. Sports Mole's predicted score is 2-2. Viking's defence is fragile: they have conceded in every recent UCL game and allowed about 2.7 xG at Villa. On the other side, Viking are very strong at home this autumn (unbeaten, 3+ goals in 7 straight home games) and will play their first-choice XI, the same one that held Bayern 3-3. They also draw rarely (2 draws in 25 league games). Sabah are predicted to make about 3 changes, have Simić doubtful, and have lost every recent away game against good sides. So the move from the market is small: home 0.68, draw 0.185, away 0.135. The straight win passes the draw ≤25% rule. Draw no bet wins about 83% of decided games (0.68/0.815) and refunds 18.5% of the time.
